title: Decouple top_k semantics from page_size and add per-item weights + explainability to rerank API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Customers building large retrieval+rerank pipelines keep asking for two competing behaviors: (1) stable, pageable result streams with a clear continuation token and fixed page_size, and (2) a top_k contract that guarantees returning the best N candidates globally (for evaluation and downstream deterministic business logic). Currently our rerank endpoint conflates page_size and top_k leading to surprising behavior when clients paginate or when we apply streaming/partial scoring optimizations.

Goals:
- Separate `top_k` (global selection budget) from `page_size` (transport/pagination chunk size).
- Allow clients to request per-item metadata: normalized weight/score, explainability features (feature contributions or highlights), and provenance pointers (doc_id / source).
- Maintain low-latency for typical 1-5 top_k use cases and scale for large top_k (1000+) with graceful degradation and explicit cost signals.
- Provide stable continuation tokens compatible with streaming and incremental rerank (so clients can resume without re-scoring all candidates).

Proposal (high-level):
1) API surface changes:
   - New request fields: `top_k` (int, optional), `page_size` (int, default 20), `cursor` (opaque string), `explain` (enum: none|minimal|full), `include_weights` (bool), `max_cost` (float) as a soft budget.
   - Response fields: `items` (list), `cursor` (optional), `meta` (string) but note: `items` elements are flat objects with keys `id`, `score`, `weight` (optional), `explain` (optional), `provenance` (optional list of strings). All values are primitive types or strings to keep payload parsable.
   - Semantics: `top_k` controls selection budget the server uses to decide which items are eligible for final sorting. `page_size` only controls how many items are returned per response. If `top_k` is omitted we treat it as unbounded for backward compatibility.

2) Server-side changes:
   - Two-phase flow: a lightweight candidate filter (embedding distance) produces M candidates; an adaptive scorer does prioritized scoring up to `top_k` budget. Scoring can be incremental and emit partial pages via `cursor`.
   - Cursor contents: an opaque base64 token encoding: generation_id, candidate_cursor (list of candidate buckets summarized as short IDs + offsets), and score-checkpoint. We'll keep token small (<= 2KB) and rotate generation_id for invalidation.
   - Explainability: `minimal` returns per-item top feature names and weights (string list), `full` returns compact serialized feature vectors (json-string) but gated behind `max_cost` and `explain=true` to limit cost.

3) Backwards compatibility and migrations:
   - Default behavior without `top_k` or `include_weights` preserves pre-existing API behavior.
   - For clients relying on previous page-based semantics, add server-side compatibility mode `legacy_paging=true` which keeps older cursor shape for 3 release cycles before deprecating.

4) Performance and cost controls:
   - Enforce soft and hard limits: `top_k` default max 1000 for hosted tier, hard max 10k for dedicated tenants with approvals. `max_cost` used to auto-throttle explain/full modes.
   - Telemetry: emit metrics per-request: requested_top_k, scanned_candidates, scored_items, explain_mode, latency_p50/p95, and cost_estimate. These feed Console panels and rollout flags.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Separating top_k and page_size increases implementation complexity (cursor state and incremental scoring) but provides deterministic evaluation semantics and clearer client ergonomics.
- Offering explainability increases latency and cost; to avoid surprising regressions we gate full explain behind `explain=full` + `max_cost` and surface warning headers when cost_estimate > threshold.
- Keeping cursor opaque simplifies evolution but requires careful versioning of token format.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API accepts `top_k` and `page_size` independently, and returns correct item counts across pages for several e2e test runs.
- Cursor resume correctness: continue from mid-stream without returning duplicates or missing top_k results (test coverage with randomized reordering and dropped pages).
- Retro-compat: existing clients (no new fields) observe <=2% latency variance.
- Observatory: console dashboard shows new metrics for a/b tests.

comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached to the Confluence doc; agreed to prioritize top_k vs page_size split for developer ergonomics. Action items: prototype cursor shape and simple explain payload.
2025-02-13 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented an initial candidate-buckets prototype. Found that naive buckets blow up token size for >5K candidates; moving to run-length compressed bucket summary.

2025-02-15 - Jing Wei (review): Requested API conservative defaults and suggested `include_weights` rather than always returning weight to keep response small by default. Concern about exposing internal score distributions as they leak calibration info.

2025-02-17 - Marco Ruiz: Benchmarks vs current endpoint: for top_k<=10 median latency 18ms (vs 22ms baseline). For top_k=500 latency increases due to scoring; added sampling-based early stop to keep p95 bounded.
2025-02-20 - PM review (Sofia Moreno): Approved MVP scope but asked for clear migration notes and an automatic compatibility flag for customers during rollout. Requested rollout plan attached to PR.

2025-02-22 - Marco Ruiz: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/1845 with feature flag gating and unit tests for cursor resume. Running integration tests on staging now. Next: instrumentation and console dashboard panels.
